AddMcpServerCommand.description:
Save an MCP server to the user settings, then restart MCP servers.

The entry has the shape of one ``mcp_servers`` settings entry. ``env`` and
``headers`` hold literal values the user entered; they are written to the
settings file and never echoed in events, errors, or this model's repr. Adding a
server is the user's decision: a frontend must show the exact command and
arguments or URL, the ``env_from`` names, and the variables ``headers_from``
sends to the URL, and have the user confirm before sending it.
AddMcpServerCommand.title: AddMcpServerCommand

BackgroundToolCallCommand.description:
Move a running foreground ``bash`` call to the background, for the user.

It runs beside the active run. The call ends with the id of the background
process it became, which tells the agent when it stops; the command fails when
no foreground ``bash`` call with this id is running.
BackgroundToolCallCommand.title: BackgroundToolCallCommand

CancelProcessCommand.description:

It runs beside any active command. The process's exit is published as
``process.ended`` with state ``cancelled``; the command fails when no running
background process has this id.

ChangeDirectoryCommand.description:
Move the session's working directory to another folder in its project.

It waits for running work and never applies in the middle of a prompt. The
reply is the saved ``session.directory_changed`` move, when one was saved,
then ``rpc.workspace`` for the new folder.

LoginMcpServerCommand.description:
Sign in to an HTTP MCP server with OAuth, then restart MCP servers.

The host opens the authorization page in the user's browser and reports it
as ``rpc.mcp.login``; the command finishes when the browser returns, the
sign-in times out, or the command is cancelled.
LoginMcpServerCommand.title: LoginMcpServerCommand

LogoutMcpServerCommand.description: Forget an MCP server's OAuth sign-in, then restart MCP servers.
LogoutMcpServerCommand.title: LogoutMcpServerCommand

MarkMcpToolsReadOnlyCommand.description:
Mark tools read-only in an MCP server's user settings, then restart MCP servers.

Marking a tool read-only lets subagents and plan mode call it,
and lets it run without approval, so it is the user's decision. ``tool_names``
are the tools the user was shown and confirmed, from the server's
``read_only_hint_tool_names`` in the ``rpc.mcp`` status. Nothing is saved unless
every one is still hinted by the running server, none already has a
`tool_safety` entry, and the server's saved settings are still the ones it was
started with.
MarkMcpToolsReadOnlyCommand.title: MarkMcpToolsReadOnlyCommand

Parse a pasted ``{"mcpServers": {...}}`` snippet without saving anything.

The reply lists each server's launch settings with environment variables named

is never echoed in events, errors, or this model's repr.
PreviewMcpSnippetCommand.title: PreviewMcpSnippetCommand

RpcMcpHeaderFrom.description:
One HTTP header whose value Wisp builds from an environment variable.

The header is sent as ``"{scheme} {value}"``, or the bare value when
``scheme`` is None. Showing it tells the user which variable's value goes to
the server.
RpcMcpHeaderFrom.title: RpcMcpHeaderFrom

RpcMcpServerLaunch.description:
What one MCP server runs or connects to, as a user must see it to confirm it.

Exactly one of ``command`` or ``url`` is set. Environment variables appear only
by name: ``env_names`` are set from values stored in the settings file, which are
never sent, and ``env_from`` are forwarded from Wisp's own environment. An HTTP
server's headers appear the same way: ``header_names`` carry stored values, and
``headers_from`` send the named variables to the server's URL.
RpcMcpServerLaunch.title: RpcMcpServerLaunch

Enable or disable an MCP server in the user settings, then restart MCP servers.

Enabling a server is the user's decision, as adding one is. ``expected`` is
required when enabling: it is the ``launch`` from the ``rpc.mcp`` status that the
user was shown and confirmed, and the server is enabled only if its saved
settings still match it.
